title: Slip of the Tongue
tagline: Something small was stolen from Case 7. The police kept quiet about what. One suspect didn't.
briefing: At 10:40 pm on Thursday the glass of display Case 7 in Harrowgate Museum's East Gallery was smashed and the case alarm went off. Whatever was inside was gone.

Inspector Kaur arrived at 11:15 and decided to keep one fact secret: what had been stolen. She interviewed each of the three staff still in the building and told every one of them exactly the same thing.
Read the interviews carefully. The thief always knows something the innocent don't.
rules: The three suspects below were the only people in the museum after 9:00 pm, apart from the police after 11:15.
Inspector Kaur told each of them only: “An item was taken from display Case 7 in the East Gallery.”

suspects.name: Victor Osei
suspects.description: Has guarded the museum for twelve years. Watches the cameras from the control room.
suspects.motive: Knows every alarm and blind spot.
suspects.statement: I was in the control room when the alarm went. The East Gallery camera has been broken for a month, I've reported it three times.

suspects.name: Rosa Quint
suspects.description: Cleans from 9 pm until midnight. Saw a delivery crate arrive that afternoon.
suspects.motive: Was recently told her hours will be cut.
suspects.statement: I was mopping the West Gallery, at the other end of the building. I heard the alarm and ran to the control room.

suspects.name: Felix Brandt
suspects.description: Was staying late for the quarterly stocktake. The gift shop is next to the East Gallery.
suspects.motive: The gift shop's takings are down and he's been warned.
suspects.statement: I was counting fridge magnets in the gift shop all evening. I've never set foot in the East Gallery tonight.

evidence.title: The curator
evidence.source: Dr. Imogen Faye, called from the museum's charity dinner at the Grand Hotel
body: “Case 7 had been empty for a week. The new piece arrived today: a small carved jade frog, about the size of a plum, on loan from a collector.”

“The courier brought it in an old reused crate stencilled CERAMICS, FRAGILE. I unpacked it myself at a quarter past six, after the staff had gone, put it in Case 7 and pulled the gallery shutter down.”
“There's no label yet, and I haven't told a soul what it is. The paperwork is locked in my office. Then I went to the dinner, where I've been all evening.”

evidence.title: Interview: Victor Osei
body: HALE: An item was taken from display Case 7 in the East Gallery.
OSEI: Case 7? That's been empty since the coin exhibition left. What was in it?
OSEI: Well, I hope it wasn't valuable. I told them about that broken camera.

evidence.title: Interview: Rosa Quint
body: HALE: An item was taken from display Case 7 in the East Gallery.
QUINT: Oh no. Was it the new thing from the crate this afternoon? It said ceramics on it. A vase, was it?
QUINT: Poor Dr. Faye. She'll be heartbroken.

evidence.title: Interview: Felix Brandt
body: HALE: An item was taken from display Case 7 in the East Gallery.
BRANDT: Well, it wasn't me. I've been in the shop all night.
BRANDT: Only the alarm. Look, why would I want a little green frog? I sell hundreds of the plastic ones for two pounds each.

evidence.title: Security company radio log
body: Scheduled radio check with the Harrowgate night guard.
10:37 pm to 10:44 pm: V. Osei on the control room radio, reading out the alarm panel status zone by zone. At 10:40 he reports: “Case 7 alarm just went off, East Gallery.”

evidence.title: UV powder check
evidence.source: Museum security policy and police check at midnight
body: Every display case is dusted with an invisible powder that glows under ultraviolet light. Anyone who touches a case gets it on their skin.
Under a UV lamp: Victor Osei, no glow. Rosa Quint, no glow. Felix Brandt, glowing powder on the fingertips of both hands and on his right cuff.

questions.prompt: Apart from the curator, who could know what was in Case 7 on Thursday night?

options.text: Anyone who worked at the museum
Only the person who smashed the case
Anyone who saw the crate arrive

questions.explanation: The frog arrived in a crate marked CERAMICS, was unpacked after staff left, had no label, and the curator told no one. Only someone who looked inside Case 7 that night could know.

questions.prompt: Which suspect knew what was stolen?
questions.explanation: Felix says “a little green frog” even though the Inspector only said “an item from Case 7”. A jade frog is small and green.

questions.prompt: Rosa mentions the crate too. Why doesn't that make her guilty?

options.text: She guessed what the crate's label said, a ceramic vase, which was wrong
She was the one who unpacked it
Cleaners aren't allowed in the East Gallery

questions.explanation: Rosa only knew what the outside of the crate said. Her guess, a vase, is wrong. That's exactly what an innocent person who saw the delivery would think.
Felix knew it was a small green frog, which only the thief could know. He has the case's UV powder on his fingertips. Victor was on a recorded radio call at 10:40.

hints.question: q1
hints.text: Read the curator's account. What did the crate say on the outside?

hints.question: q1
hints.text: Was there a label? Did she tell anyone?

hints.question: q1
hints.text: The crate lied, there was no label and nobody was told. You'd have to see inside the case.

hints.question: q2
hints.text: Compare what the Inspector said with what each person said back.

hints.question: q2
hints.text: Someone describes the stolen item. Who?

hints.question: q2
hints.text: “A little green frog.” Who told him it was green, or a frog?

hints.question: q3
hints.text: Is what Rosa says actually right?

hints.question: q3
hints.text: Compare her guess with what was really in the case.

hints.question: q3
hints.text: She guessed from the outside of the crate, and got it wrong. That's innocent.

hints.question: q4
hints.text: Check each suspect's whereabouts at 10:40 and anything they touched.

hints.question: q4
hints.text: One suspect was on a recorded radio call. The UV lamp tells you about the other two.

hints.question: q4
hints.text: Glowing fingertips and a slip about a green frog. Case closed?

solution.summary: Felix Brandt slipped out of the gift shop, ducked under the East Gallery shutter and smashed Case 7, expecting something he could sell. He found a small jade frog and pocketed it. In his interview he tried to sound bored and gave himself away: nobody had told him the stolen item was a frog, or that it was green.

chain.step: Only the curator and whoever looked into Case 7 that night could know what was in it.
The Inspector told everyone only “an item from Case 7”.
Felix called it “a little green frog”. Rosa guessed a vase from the crate label. Victor didn't know the case was full.
Victor was on a recorded radio check at 10:40. Felix has the case's UV powder on his fingers.

eliminations.why: On a recorded radio call with the alarm company from 10:37 to 10:44, reporting the alarm as it happened. No UV powder.
She only knew the crate's misleading label and guessed wrong. No UV powder.

playtest.solvePath: Solvers read the three interviews side by side. About half spot 'green frog' straight away; the rest find it after the level-2 hint. Rosa's crate comment is a good fake-out for those who rush.
pitfalls: Early on, players argued Felix could have seen the frog through the gallery doorway earlier. The curator now says she installed it after staff left and pulled the shutter down.
Some suspected Victor because of the broken camera. The radio log clears him.
revisions: Made the crate say CERAMICS so that seeing the delivery tells you nothing true.
Added the UV powder so the case isn't decided on one slip of the tongue alone.
Stated in the rules that the Inspector told all three exactly the same sentence.
